holidays.name: Black Cat Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate sleek, shadowy felines. It's also a day to remind people that a black coat doesn't make a cat any less lovable. Adopt one, snap a photo, or give your resident panther-in-miniature some extra treats.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance created by cat lovers to counter the superstitions that have long followed black cats. Its exact origin is unclear. It aims to boost adoption rates for black cats, who are often overlooked in shelters.
holidays.funFact: In the United Kingdom and Japan, black cats are traditionally seen as symbols of good luck, not bad omens.

holidays.name: National I Love My Feet Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the two hardworking appendages that carry you through life. Celebrate with a foot soak, a massage, fresh socks, or a barefoot stroll through the grass.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to pay attention to foot health and give their feet some well-earned pampering.
holidays.funFact: Each human foot has 26 bones, so your two feet hold about a quarter of all the bones in your body.

holidays.name: National Thrift Shop Day
holidays.description: A salute to secondhand shopping, where bargain hunters can find vintage jackets, quirky mugs, and mystery treasures at tiny prices. Many thrift shops are run by charities, so your finds can support a good cause and keep usable goods out of landfills.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates thrift stores and the people who shop and donate there.
holidays.funFact: Thrifting is one of the easiest ways to shop sustainably, because every secondhand item you buy is one that doesn't have to be newly made.
